summary_paraphrase: A boy dreams of a parade of Indian sweets. Each sweet gets a short rhyming verse that hands over to the next one, often through a question. After the warmest sweet he wakes with a start on a rooftop cot at night, calls the sweets back, shuts his eyes and returns to the dream to dance with them.

humor_notes: Wordplay and absurd images of sweets as royalty and vehicles; the cat's play is a picture joke.

repetition.description: each sweet gets a verse opening with its name said twice, then hands over to the next sweet
repetition.why: a predictable chant that a listener can join; the hand-over makes each page turn expected

repetition.description: the waking page lists all the sweets again
repetition.why: gathers the whole dream back before sleep

repetition.description: the last page returns to the dream world of the first
repetition.why: closes the circle: dream, wake, dream

notes: Only the waking picture shows the real setting: a rope cot on a rooftop at night, and that the dream cat is his own cat.
The two night pages (12-13) are the only dark pages; colour carries the dream/waking change.
On p9 Faizu already floats with closed eyes: the picture prepares the waking.

strengths: A chant structure that hands each page to the next (question or named next sweet): strong anticipation for a read-aloud.
The real-world turn comes late (p12 of 14) and is quickly soothed; the book ends inside sleep.
A rhyme that completes across the page turn (p11 to p12) makes the waking the strongest turn.
weaknesses: Almost no story problem until p12; the middle is a list.
Food words (Indian sweets) need context for readers outside India.

anti_patterns.note: verse pages that only add a sweet without moving anything

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Bedtime dream book; brief waking start (research 2/5, about 1 on the engine's 0-3 scale). As a text-only model the rooftop and the real cat would need to be told in words (m005).

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
